old: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and most were not short of vitamin D.
new: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D.
reason: Fact-check major: Attributes 'mostly not short of vitamin D' to both trials; baseline vitamin D status for D-Health was not verified (claim C04-20-c qualification forbids it). Only VITAL is supported.

new: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D.
reason: Fact-check major: Attributes 'mostly not short of vitamin D' to both trials; baseline vitamin D status for D-Health was not verified (claim C04-20-c qualification forbids it). Only VITAL is supported.

old: Most were healthy and not short of vitamin D.
new: Most were healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D.
reason: Fact-check major: Same overstatement applied to all 45,000 across both trials.

old: Most people in them were healthy and not short of vitamin D.

old: Vitamin D with calcium slightly cut hip fractures in pooled trials, more so in care homes.
new: Vitamin D with calcium slightly cut hip fractures in pooled trials; because hip fractures are more common in care homes, more are estimated to be prevented there.
reason: Fact-check minor: 'More so' implies a larger effect in care homes; the per-1000 figures apply one pooled relative risk to a higher assumed baseline risk.

old: For approved drugs, density gains do track fracture reduction across whole trials. In one person, much less so: with alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures.
new: For approved drugs, density gains do track fracture reduction across whole trials. But density explains only part of the benefit: with alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures. And a repeat scan in one person varies more than the real differences between people.
reason: Fact-check major: The 16% is a trial-level proportion of the alendronate benefit explained by spine density, not a measure of how well density predicts benefit in one person. Presents a trial-level statistic as individual-level evidence.

old: In one person it explains little: with alendronate, about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures.
new: But density explains only part of the benefit: with alendronate, about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures. One person's repeat scan varies more than the real differences between people.
reason: Fact-check major: Same conflation of a trial-level proportion with an individual prediction.

old: In one person it is a weaker guide. With alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures.
new: It also explains only part of the benefit: with alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures. In one person it is a weaker guide still.
reason: Fact-check minor: Presents the 16% as evidence about individuals.

old: In 1990, fluoride raised spine density by 35% but did not cut spinal fractures; other fractures rose (72 v 24).
new: In a 1990 trial, fluoride raised spine density 35% more than placebo but did not cut spinal fractures; there were more other fractures (72 v 24 fractures).
reason: Fact-check minor: 'Rose' implies a within-arm increase; 72 v 24 is a between-group count of fractures, not women. Missing 'more than placebo'.

old: In US records, 19 in 100 men treated had broken a bone after 5 years, against 13 in 100 untreated, a link rather than proof.
new: In US records of men with prostate cancer who lived at least 5 years, 19 in 100 who had hormone treatment had broken a bone, against 13 in 100 who did not, a link rather than proof.
reason: Fact-check major: Figures apply only to men with prostate cancer who survived at least 5 years after diagnosis (a subgroup), not a 5-year cumulative risk for all treated men.

old: Men, 5 years on: 19 in 100 treated v 13 in 100 untreated broke a bone (link, not proof)
new: Men with prostate cancer who lived 5+ years: 19 in 100 with hormone treatment v 13 in 100 without had broken a bone (link, not proof)
reason: Fact-check major: Same subgroup presented as a 5-year risk.

old: Men, 5 years on: 19 in 100 treated v 13 in 100 untreated broke a bone (link, not proof)
new: Men with prostate cancer who lived 5+ years: 19 in 100 with hormone treatment v 13 in 100 without had broken a bone (link, not proof)
reason: Fact-check major: Same subgroup presented as a 5-year risk.

old: Among men surviving 5 years, 19 in 100 treated v 13 in 100 untreated broke a bone (observational).
new: Among men with prostate cancer who lived at least 5 years, 19 in 100 who had hormone treatment v 13 in 100 who did not had broken a bone (observational).
reason: Fact-check minor: Should say 'at least 5 years' and 'with prostate cancer'.

old: In trials, a year of bisphosphonate treatment spared about 1 in 100 women a non-spinal fracture. For someone likely to live only months, the weekly tablet routine may not help in time. Stopping can be right.
new: In trials of women aged 63 to 74 on average, a year of bisphosphonate treatment spared about 1 in 100 a non-spinal fracture. For someone likely to live only months, the weekly tablet routine may not help in time. Stopping can be right.
reason: Fact-check minor: Omits the necessary qualification that trial women were 63 to 74 and not near the end of life; short version generalises.

old: The balance stays favourable: an estimated 149 hip fractures prevented for 2 atypical fractures per 10,000 White women over 3 years.
new: The balance stays favourable: modelled estimates give 149 hip fractures prevented for 2 atypical fractures per 10,000 White women with osteoporosis over 3 years (less favourable, but still positive, in Asian women).
reason: Fact-check minor: Missing that these are modelled estimates for women with osteoporosis, and that the balance was less favourable in Asian women.
